subject: POC success metrics and sprint decomposition — Loomly trial
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@loomly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post‑call recap + proposed success slate and sprint decomposition

Hi Ava — thanks for a great discussion this morning. Quick recap and my proposed practical next steps for the 4‑week POC we discussed. I want to make sure we all agree on what 'success' looks like and who owns each evaluation lane so we can start the workstream next Monday.

Call recap (30m):
- Primary use case: document summarization + in‑app assistant for content editors (batch and interactive).
- Expected trial volume: ~80k tokens/day peak; interactive sessions ~150–250 QPS concurrent bursts.
- Key constraints: p95 latency target, cost per token budget, and generation quality (precision of entity extraction + factuality).

Proposed success criteria (high level):
1) Latency: end‑to‑end p95 ≤ 250ms for interactive flows (95th measured at request level, excluding frontend render).
2) Throughput: sustained 200 QPS for short inference (<512 tokens) with <10% error/retry rate under synthetic load.
3) Cost: average server cost ≤ $0.0008 per token across test set (baseline measured on our hosted variant).
4) Quality: 90% of sampled prompts meet acceptance thresholds — defined as: ROUGE‑L ≥ 0.68 on the summarization holdout, and entity extraction precision ≥ 0.92 on the QA set.

Evaluation plan (recommended):
- Dataset: Loomly to share a 2k example holdout (mix of short/long docs) + 200 labeled examples for entity QA. (Attachment: loomly_sample_payloads_v1.csv)
- Runs: 3 runs over 7 days each (baseline model, quantized variant, and caching/batch enabled) to measure variability.
- Metrics capture: token counts, server CPU/GPU utilization, p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost. Redwood will provide a dashboard link and raw CSVs.
- Ownership: Redwood to run initial baseline and supply perf artifacts; Loomly to validate quality on labeled set.

Sprint decomposition & timeline (target start Mon 2028‑07‑31):
- Week 1 (kickoff + data ingest): attach sample payloads, map routes, enable observability. Owners: Karthik (AE) / Monica (Solutions Eng).
- Week 2 (baseline runs): Redwood executes baseline and reports perf. Owners: Monica / Ben.
- Week 3 (ops tuning + quantization): try quantized variant and caching. Owners: Ben / Monica.
- Week 4 (quality readout and decision): joint readout, sign off or extension. Owners: Karthik / Loomly PM.

Ask for Loomly before EOD Friday:
1) Confirm the holdout and QA samples share (CSV or Drive link).
2) Confirm procurement timeline (Procurement contact copied).
3) Any non‑standard compliance constraints (data residency, logging retention).

Attachments: redwood_poc_sprint_matrix.xlsx (workback schedule), loomly_sample_payloads_v1.csv

Thanks — I’ll draft a one‑page mutual action plan once you confirm the datasets and procurement timeline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0147

From: Ava Reynolds <ava@loomly.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@loomly.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post‑call recap + proposed success slate and sprint decomposition

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear writeup and timeline. Agreeable overall, a few quick notes from our side: 

- We can deliver the 2k holdout and 200 QA samples by Monday morning (sharing via Drive). I’ll drop the link to the folder in a follow up.
- Latency target sounds tight but reasonable for the interactive path — important for our UX. Can you confirm whether the p95 target is with or without network? We prefer end‑to‑end to include our client serialization so the number is actionable for engineering.
- Cost: Loomly’s procurement prefers a not‑to‑exceed cost line item in the MSA. Procurement looped in.

Procurement note: We need a draft of the commercial term sheet and a high‑level data handling note to start our internal review. If you can share the term sketch by Monday, that helps our approvers.

Thanks — I’ll upload the data and invite your team to the Drive folder.

— Ava
Ava Reynolds | Head of Product, Loomly
ava@loomly.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post‑call recap + proposed success slate and sprint decomposition

Karthik — quick technical clarifications for the sprint plan so we’re ready once Loomly shares payloads: 

1) Measurement method: we’ll report p95 using server‑side timestamps (ingress → egress). If Loomly wants client‑side included, we can add that as a separate column but baseline will be server‑side. (Ava — noted).
2) Throughput test: we’ll run a controlled synthetic load from our EU and US load generators to validate cross‑region behavior.
3) Cost calc: we’ll provide token accounting per request (tokenize on both sides) + estimated infra cost scoped to the committed trial period.
4) Failure budget: propose an ops gate of ≤10% retries/errors across the baseline runs; if above, we won’t mark the run valid.

Also — Lauren I’ll need the sample dashboard template and the gating checklist you used for the previous trial (can you attach to Drive in the shared folder?). Monica, can you take point for the baseline run next Tuesday and confirm GPU flavor?

— Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Reynolds <ava@loomly.ai>, Procurement <procure@loomly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post‑call recap + proposed success slate and sprint decomposition

Ava — great, thanks. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- Loomly data: I got the Drive invite (thanks) and pulled loomly_sample_payloads_v1.csv. Monica will validate schema tonight.
- p95 definition: we will publish both server‑side (our default baseline) and end‑to‑end (client‑side) p95 columns. For the success gate use server‑side p95 ≤ 250ms unless Loomly explicitly requests end‑to‑end as the acceptance metric. Please state preference by Tuesday EOD.
- Commercials & procurement: attaching a one‑page term sketch (po_terms_draft.docx). Karthik (AE) to own the commercial follow up; Procurement please share your standard PO/CL request window.
- Owners & milestones (confirming):
  • Data ingest + workback (Week 1): Loomly (Ava) + Karthik/Monica (Redwood)
  • Baseline perf (Week 2): Monica & Ben (Redwood)
  • Ops tuning (Week 3): Ben (lead) with Redwood infra
  • Quality readout (Week 4): Loomly product + Redwood (joint)

Next actions (this week):
1) Redwood: upload dashboard template + gating checklist to Drive (Lauren).
2) Loomly: confirm whether they want server‑side or end‑to‑end p95 as the formal acceptance metric (Ava).
3) Procurement: initial term feedback on sketch by Tue EOD or indicate review timeline.

I’ll turn this into a mutual action plan doc and share tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone — excited to get started.

— Karthik

Redwood Inference
